narration: Welcome to the Harappan and Early Historic India gallery. Here we have a Painted Grey Ware bowl, accession number NM 68.7/12, dating from about 1200 to 600 BCE, found in the Ganga‑Yamuna plain. It is a small fired‑clay vessel, 14 centimetres in diameter, with simple black painted bands near the rim—typical of the Painted Grey Ware tradition. While we don’t yet have a full curator write‑up, these bowls are thought to have been everyday utilitarian items, perhaps used for cooking or storage. If you’d like to learn more about how such vessels were used in daily life, feel free to ask the staff for further details.
